title: Explainable Charge & Latency Engine — deterministic per-route/model/customer breakdowns
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers and internal teams need an auditable, explainable breakdown of inference cost and latency that ties every billed token and observed latency segment back to route, model variant, and customer. Current rollups intermix inference runtime, queuing, and upstream processing and lack deterministic attribution for cached prefixes, fallbacks, and multi-model fanouts.

Goal: Build a cost & latency computation engine that produces deterministic, queryable breakdowns per-route/model/customer with explainability metadata (attribution reasons, contribution shares, and confidence), supports near-real-time dashboards, and is suitable for downstream chargeback and SLA reconciliation.

Success criteria:
- Accuracy: unit test coverage and reconciliations within 0.5% for common traffic patterns and documented divergence bounds for edge cases (fallbacks, truncated traces).
- Latency: allow 5–10 minute freshness for operational dashboards; hourly materializations for billing.
- Explainability: every aggregated row includes a short reason code string and contributing event ids for sampling-based audit.
- Cost: incremental storage <10% of current telemetry table growth using partitioned materialized views and compact encodings.

Scope: ingestion adapters, attribution engine, materialized views, reconciliation jobs, API for queries, Grafana dashboards, and runbook. Does not include billing pipeline ingestion (handled by finance) but will provide export artifacts for that pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end test that reproduces token-level attribution for a synthetic route with prefix caching and a model fanout; breakdown matches golden file
Operational dashboard shows per-route P50/P95 token latency and cost per 1K tokens with 10-minute freshness
Backfill completed for last 90 days with validated reconciliation report comparing to baseline rollups
Explainability metadata surfaceable via console drilldown (reason codes and sample trace ids)
approach:
We will compute a join of enriched request traces (request metadata + model variant + route + customer + token counts + cache hit flags) with runtime profiling records (per-stage durations: queue, compute, io, serialize). Two complementary execution patterns: (A) streaming aggregator for near-real-time dashboards using Flink/Materialize-style incremental aggregates and (B) periodic batch materializations for hourly and billing artifacts. Attribution rules are deterministic functions implemented in SQL UDFs: token-weighted cost allocation for shared GPU batches, and stage-weighted latency attribution for multi-stage requests. We'll include provenance fields to support audits.

Storage design: time-partitioned materialized views in BigQuery/Postgres-OLAP (depending on infra), compacting reason codes and enumerated model ids into int enums to save bytes. We plan a single canonical materialized table per day with pre-aggregated keys: date, hour, route_id, model_id, customer_id, reason_code. Detailed trace samples will be kept in a low-cost archive bucket with pointers from aggregated rows.

Trade-offs considered: full token-level joins are accurate but expensive; we will use deterministic summarization at ingress (token counts + cache flags) to avoid huge joins. For tail latency we will sample 1% of traces to capture exact stage timings and extrapolate with confidence intervals.
implementation_tasks: Schema: define canonical enrichment schema and reason_code taxonomy (ENG-70213-schema-v1)
Ingestion: implement adapter from telemetry Kafka topic to enrichment stream and add deterministic summarizers (cache flags, token deltas)
Aggregator: build streaming aggregator job (Flink) to emit 10-minute aggregates and write to materialized view
Batch: create hourly batch materializer and backfill job with failure handling and idempotency
API: surface a read API and SQL views for console queries and billing export
Monitoring: add reconciliation job that compares new aggregates to legacy rollups and emits drift alerts
Dashboard: Grafana panels + console drilldown to show explainability metadata and sample traces
Runbook: incident runbook for stale aggregates and reconciliation failures

risks_mitigations: Risk: Backfill and retention could spike storage costs. Mitigation: use enum compression, time-partitioned compaction, and archive raw traces to cold storage after 30 days
Risk: Attribution logic divergence vs billing pipeline. Mitigation: weekly reconciliations and a signed artifact export for finance; add reconciliation thresholds and alerts
Risk: High cardinality of routes/models causing slow queries. Mitigation: pre-aggregate common rollups and add shard keys; advise console to limit ad-hoc queries to peak top-N
Risk: Real-time streaming accuracy for cached prefixes. Mitigation: treat prefix cache hits as separate reason_code and surface sample traces for audit
testing_plan: Unit tests for SQL UDFs and attribution rules
Integration test injecting synthetic traces that exercise fanout, fallback, and cache-hit scenarios; compare against golden file
Canary: 2-week canary with customers A and B; run live reconciliation every 6 hours
Load test: run backfill at 3x expected daily ingest to verify compaction and job stability
